channel.title: supermemory — Writing
channel.description: Engineering notes, technical reports, and announcements from the supermemory team.

item.title: We're open sourcing the company brain. Here's how we designed the multiplayer harness
item.description: Company Brain is now open source. A walkthrough of the multiplayer harness behind its Slack experience, from proactivity and memory boundaries to approvals and recovery.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: Jev changes a lot in memory & context engineering. Here's exactly how.
item.description: We tested Jev across reranking, chunking, observation, and harness decisions. Here is where fast decision models help memory systems, where they cost more, and where they still fall short.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: I reverse-engineered Instinct's memory. Here's exactly how it works
item.description: Instinct keeps its memory as git-tracked markdown files, found with grep rather than vectors. Here is the whole system as far as black-box probing can reconstruct it, and how to rebuild it on supermemory in about 60 lines.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: An update to supermemory
item.description: We've discontinued the supermemory company brain and Nova. Everyone who was charged has been refunded, our MCP and plugins continue to run, and we're going all in on the memory engine.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: Scaling Conversations: How Adapta Grew Usage Without Losing Context
item.description: Adapta added Supermemory as a persistent memory layer so every conversation keeps its context — letting the team scale usage without losing the thread.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: How Chatarmin Ditched RAG and Went Memory-Only with Supermemory
item.description: Chatarmin replaced a heavy RAG pipeline with Supermemory's memory layer — cutting average AI response time from 40s to 12s and token usage by 40–50%.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: SMFS: making agentic retrieval 55% cheaper AND more accurate
item.description: We launched SMFS.ai (Supermemory Filesystem) a few weeks ago, with a simple bet: We can redesign the filesystem specifically for agents, with special files, structures, and commands that it can use for it's tasks. Today, SMFS is used by hundreds of companies to power their agents.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: Introducing Dynamic Dreaming: supermemory now connects the dots, for you.
item.description: Dreaming is magical. TLDR: We're launching Dynamic Dreaming in supermemory today, which automatically works if you're using supermemory in any way - API, OpenClaw, Hermes agent, etc.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: Dear reader, we just made supermemory insanely cheap... the Context Cloud
item.description: When I first started building supermemory, I had one goal: To build the best memory system for AI. I would talk to customers, and find out that memory was not the only thing they needed - They were all setting up 7-8 different vendors at the same time.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: Introducing @supermemory/tools v2.0.0
item.description: Today we're releasing v2.0.0. This release unifies the API across all agents sdk integrations from AI SDK to Mastra, makes conversation identity a first-class concept, and ships with memory saving on by default.
item.author: Mahesh Sanikommu

item.title: Solving the Precision-Recall Tradeoff: Search Result Aggregation
item.description: When you're building memory for AI, search is your foundational layer. The way search generally works is straightforward: the user defines a query, and then sets a limit (top-K) on how many search results they want returned. Usually, this is set to 10 or 20.
item.author: Soham Daga

item.title: OpenClaw Memory Problems: Why It Forgets and How to Fix It (2026)
item.description: TLDR: Today, we are releasing a new version of our openclaw plugin - https://github.com/supermemoryai/openclaw-supermemory. This post is going to be a bit technical, so bear with me (or bookmark for later!) In this post, I will talk about what we do about OpenClaw memory, and how we fix it.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: Stateful Coding Agents with Memory: Build Long-Running Agents (2026)
item.description: We built a plugin for Claude Code and OpenCode that gives your coding agent persistent memory. It remembers your preferences, learns your codebase, and never loses context mid-conversation. The result is an agent you can run for months without starting over.
item.author: Shoubhit

item.title: Clawd / Molt bot's memory SUCKS. We gave it supermemory.
item.description: I'm the founder of supermemory. Clawd/Molt bot is blowing up right now, with many, many use cases. I set it up, too, and have been using it through telegram. TLDR: just go to /docs/integrations/clawdbot to set up supermemory for your clawd bot.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: Catch up with our UNFORGETTABLE Launch Week
item.description: Over the last year, one belief has guided almost everything we’ve built at Supermemory AI becomes meaningfully useful only when it remembers. Memory shouldn’t be something developers rebuild from scratch. It shouldn’t be fragile, expensive, or trapped inside a single tool.
item.author: Shardul Mane

item.title: Empowering the Next Generation of Founders: Supermemory Startup Program
item.description: If there’s one thing we’ve learned while building Supermemory, it’s that most startups don’t fail because they didn't build features; they fail when infrastructure slows them down, or they built too slow.
item.author: Shardul Mane

item.title: Building code-chunk: AST Aware Code Chunking
item.description: At Supermemory, we're building context engineering infrastructure for AI. A huge part of that is dealing with code: ingesting repos, understanding structure, and making it searchable. The problem is that most code chunking solutions are terrible. We built code-chunk to fix this.
item.author: Shoubhit

item.title: Supermemory raises $3 million with the best memory engine for LLMs
item.description: Today, I am excited to announce our first funding round to accelerate our mission of building an interoperable, scalable and reliable memory for LLMs and agents. Memory is one of the hardest challenges in AI right now.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: Mem0 vs Supermemory: Why Scira Switched
item.description: Scira AI moved its production memory layer from Mem0 to Supermemory. This is what failed, what improved, and how the team evaluated the two systems.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: Never Record Again: How Montra Uses Supermemory to Rethink Video Creation
item.description: Campbell Baron, the founder of Montra, has been making videos since he was twelve. By thirteen, he was already doing brand work. Today, he’s betting on a very different future for creators: a world where recording is the exception, and most videos are generated from scratch.
item.author: Naman Bansal

item.title: Unified Memory That Works Where You Work: Your Second Brain With Supermemory
item.description: Hi everyone, I’m Dhravya, the founder of Supermemory. I want to start with a little story behind why this product means so much to me. You can also skip straight to what it is and how it works below.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: Supermemory just got faster on PlanetScale
item.description: What is Supermemory? Supermemory completes the missing part of the LLM puzzle: memory. Just as memory is crucial for human intelligence, it's essential for truly intelligent AI systems.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: Faster, smarter, reliable infinite chat: Supermemory IS context engineering.
item.description: People are obsessed with prompts and prompt engineering. Sure, what you say is important, but what the model knows when you say it is the difference between a stateless text generator and an intelligent AI system. In short, context is the most crucial component.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: We solved AI API interoperability
item.description: One API to rule them all, One spec to find them, One library to bring them all and in the TypeScript, bind them. When we were building the Infinite Chat API, initially, we only supported the OpenAI format. This was fine, until a lot of our customers started asking for more.
item.author: Alex Foster

item.title: The Wow Factor of Memory - How Flow Used Supermemory To Build Smarter, Stickier Products
item.description: Overview: Flow is a note-taking app built around a bold vision: to create a more personal, context-aware writing experience powered by AI. At the heart of this mission is memory.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: The UX and technicalities of awesome MCPs
item.description: Last month, we launched the Supermemory MCP, mostly to test our own infrastructure and get some initial traction. It blew up. To my absolute surprise, the initial launch itself got half a million impressions (!!!). Then, we launched and got #2 on ProductHunt too.
item.author: Dhravya Shah

item.title: Architecting a memory engine inspired by the human brain
item.description: Language is at the heart of intelligence, but what truly powers meaningful interaction is memory — the ability to accumulate, recall, and contextualize information over time. Large Language Models (LLMs) have mastered language, but memory remains their Achilles’ heel.
item.author: Dhravya Shah
